title: dbo benchmark result
description: One run. The machine is recorded with the numbers because a figure without its hardware is unattributable, and a Pi 4 and a Pi 5 differ by two to three times.

profile.description: ram = PGDATA on tmpfs: a CPU and concurrency ceiling, NOT a storage figure, because fsync is free. nvme = what a deployment feels. existing = a PostgreSQL the bench did not provision, on a disk it does not have to itself: comparable with its own earlier runs and with nothing else.

thermal.description: Sampled throughout. A run whose throttle flags latched is reported, not hidden — its numbers describe cooling rather than code.

valid.description: False when the run throttled, when any request failed, or when the machine could not be watched at all (no vcgencmd — a laptop or a CI container). An invalid run is kept and marked, never quietly dropped; it simply may not be quoted.

coldStartMs.description: Distribution boot to the first 200 on a current schema.

writeWithPdi.description: The same path with personal-data isolation on. The delta is the per-write cost of encrypting identifying elements.

tokenLookup.description: identifier=system|value — 88 of 206 measured production call sites are this one shape, so it is weighted as reality weights it.

feedLagMs.description: Consumer lag across every tenant database under write load. The differentiated measurement: N tenant databases on one instance is exactly what the commit-fence fast path exists for.

tenantsBeforeDegradation.description: How many tenants one JVM holds before latency leaves its band. A product limit an edge deployment has to be told.

stepPhasesMs.description: Where a step run's time went. Every activity in a deployment is a step run, and a run is not one duration: retrieve is fetching what it works on — on a person's record also decrypting it — execute is the service's own time, write is closing the run and releasing the claim. Which phase dominates decides what to do about a slow deployment; the whole hides that.

provisioningMs.description: What a tenant costs to bring up, phase by phase, read from the deployment's own bring-up runs rather than timed from outside. toServingMs is wall clock from the declaration appearing to the tenant answering; the rest are the phases beneath it — serve is the whole, database is creating it, face and zone are synchronising definitions from wherever they come from, vocabulary is loading one. A total tells an operator that provisioning takes half a minute and nothing about which half to attack.

failures.description: Requests that did not succeed, by status. Any failure makes the run invalid: a latency figure over the requests that happened to work is not a figure about the system, and it errs flatteringly, because the requests that break tend to be the slow ones.
